articles.title: Green Solution Technology eyes substitution gains as foreign power IC prices rise, plans 7% hike in 4Q26
articles.short_snippet: Green Solution Technology is pursuing opportunities to replace international suppliers in the high-end power management IC (PMIC) market as those suppliers raise prices, while preparing a further price increase of about 7% in the fourth quarter of 2026. articles.title: Analysis: Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia, but he is returning to a changed board
articles.short_snippet: Nvidia's board took six days to go from ruling out Jensen Huang's return to reinstating him. Despite that, its own filings show the founder will be coming back to a different company. Nvidia now has its first board chair, an ongoing investigation, and a new layer of national security oversight. All three took shape while Huang was gone.

articles.title: IPC makers see no AI project delays after US midterms as edge server inquiries rise
articles.short_snippet: Several industrial PC (IPC) makers said their AI-related projects are proceeding as planned, with no clear delays so far, even as the market reassesses the returns on heavy AI spending by cloud service providers (CSPs) amid uncertainty over US energy and AI policy following the midterm elections. Some said customer inquiries for edge servers have increased.

articles.title: Sarvam's foreign-model platform tests India's AI-sovereignty goals
articles.short_snippet: Sarvam's decision to host Chinese-developed AI models on Indian infrastructure is putting a practical question at the center of India's push for technological independence: whether sovereignty depends on owning the models, controlling the computing infrastructure, or both.

articles.title: Rene Haas, once touted as possible Nvidia successor, commits to lead Arm to 2033
articles.short_snippet: Arm CEO Rene Haas has confirmed that he will extend his leadership of the company under a new agreement lasting until 2033. Previously, he had been considered a top contender to lead Nvidia after the resignation of Jensen Huang, who has since been reinstated as CEO.

articles.title: Analysis: Jensen Huang's return divides China's AI industry over Nvidia dependence
articles.short_snippet: Less than two weeks after China's technology industry began contemplating a "post-Jensen era," Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO on November 23 has upended expectations. Chinese companies tied to the global AI server supply chain stand to benefit from renewed confidence in Nvidia's technology roadmap, while domestic GPU developers could face weaker near-term substitution expectations. articles.title: Samsung cuts executive promotions by 19%, favors chip division
articles.short_snippet: Samsung Electronics cut annual executive promotions by nearly a fifth. However, its semiconductor division saw more promotions, rewarding engineers behind its high-bandwidth memory (HBM) business and foundry specialists responsible for securing orders and improving manufacturing yields.

articles.title: Taiwan clears initial funding to launch homegrown Albatross II drone production
articles.short_snippet: Taiwan's domestically developed Albatross II military drone has cleared a major funding hurdle, paving the way for initial production after the Legislative Yuan approved NT$1.675 billion (US$50.96 million) in first-year funding under the central government's 2026 supplementary budget. articles.title: Samsung targets fivefold increase in V9 NAND capacity in China
articles.short_snippet: Samsung Electronics plans to boost production capacity for its ninth-generation (V9) NAND flash memory fivefold at its second plant in Xi'an, China, by November 2027 to meet demand for enterprise solid-state drives (eSSDs) used in AI data centers, Seoul Economic Daily reported, citing industry sources.

articles.title: Ukraine defense tech firm Uforce raises US$700 million, eyes Asia-Pacific production, Taiwan suppliers
articles.short_snippet: Uforce, a defense technology company founded in Ukraine and headquartered in the UK, announced the completion of a US$700 million Series A funding round. The funding will be used to help the company expand research and development of its unmanned systems, as well as support efforts to move production facilities closer to frontline markets.

articles.title: Cisco, OpenAI launch open-source project to counter AI-driven cyberattacks
articles.short_snippet: Cisco Systems and OpenAI have launched an open-source cybersecurity project designed to protect running Linux systems from attacks while permanent software patches are being developed.

articles.title: Macronix bets on 3D NAND and NOR as bigger rivals retreat from low-capacity markets
articles.short_snippet: Macronix International is betting on 3D NAND and 3D NOR flash memory to drive its next phase of growth as major global memory manufacturers withdraw from low- and mid-capacity markets, leaving opportunities in automotive and other specialty applications.

articles.title: SpaceX prices US$44 billion Nvidia chip financing, with most debt yielding above 8%
articles.short_snippet: SpaceX has priced about US$44 billion in financing tied to Nvidia chips, with most of the roughly US$32 billion in debt notes yielding more than 8%—well above typical investment-grade levels and a sign that investors remain wary of whether heavy AI spending will pay off, according to Bloomberg and Quartz .

articles.title: Rocket startup Stoke Space challenges SpaceX with fully reusable rocket technology, targeting 2027 debut
articles.short_snippet: Competition in the US commercial space launch market is intensifying as Stoke Space, a rocket startup founded just seven years ago, seeks to challenge SpaceX with technology designed to make an entire launch vehicle reusable.

articles.title: Smart ring shipments near 5 million, but AI glasses could unlock the next growth wave
articles.short_snippet: Global smart ring shipments are projected to approach five million units in 2026, up from around four million in 2025, according to industry estimates. While the market remains dwarfed by smartwatches and Bluetooth earbuds, whose annual shipments exceed 100 million units, emerging applications in AI, mobile payments, and smart glasses integration could accelerate adoption.

articles.title: AI chip cooling shifts to diamond copper, but machining remains a major bottleneck
articles.short_snippet: Rising thermal design power and expanding die sizes in AI server chips are pushing thermal architectures from two thermal interface material (TIM) layers down to one, while driving a material shift from traditional copper to diamond copper. However, thermal solution providers warn that machining difficulties remain the biggest bottleneck, preventing large-scale adoption for now.

articles.short_snippet: Shanghai HiSilicon has launched and begun mass production of its 8MP intelligent CMOS image sensor (CIS), the CS6286, targeting dashboard cameras and parking surveillance systems. articles.short_snippet: Power management IC (PMIC) designer Green Solution Technology has secured positions in the supply chains of Nvidia, AMD, Lenovo and Nintendo through its integrated buck converters, high-current power solutions and customised designs. articles.short_snippet: DIGITIMES Intelligence observed that the agentic AI ecosystem will mature further in 2027, encompassing upstream large language models (LLMs) and computing hardware; midstream monitoring, tracking, and cybersecurity protection; as well as downstream enterprise workflow and productivity applications.
